Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

APPENDIX A 

( Clause 4 ) 

RECOMMENDED COMPOUNDING INGREDIENTS 

A*1. Gonoral — In giving the following data it is not intended to imply that the use of alternative 
materials may not give belts of a suitable quality. The recommendations are, in every case, intended 
mainly to indicate types of materials which have been found, by practical experience, to be suitable 
for producing belts to be used for conveying foodstuffs. 

A-2. Compounding 

A-2.1 The belts may be made from natural rubber, or some suitable synthetic non-toxic elastomer 
or a blond of the two together with the necessary compounding ingredients. 

A*2^ All the compounding ingredients used in the rubber shall be free from harmful materials liable 
to extraction by contact with foodstuffs or which may cause the development of undesirable odour, 
taste or discolouration. 

Neta •— In the case of natural rubber belts, light coloured crepe of natural ruboer that has been rendered suitable 
for extrusion (superior processing rubber), or air-dried plantation rubber that is free from p-nitrophenoi ( so called 
air-dried aheets ), and in the case of synthetic rubber belts, c/s-1, 4-polyisoprene, poiybutadiene, styrene-butadiene 
copolymers, nitrile-butadfene copolymers or chioroprene rubber ( polychloroprene), or a blend of any of these, may 
be used as raw nwterial. Divinyl benzene may be used as third polymerization component. 

A-3. Acoalaratort— Recommended accelerators of the tasteless type to suit the requirements 
speclflsd In 4aro thiuram disulphides or monosulphides, dithiocarbamates and suitable polyamines. 

A-4. Antioxidants «-> Where jt Is considered that an antioxidant be employed, the following materials 
are recommended. 

A-4.1 Cond9nM9tton Products of Acetone end Aniline 

A'4.2 Dh^nepfdhyl-p'pfienylenedfam/ne ( Symmetric ) 

A«S. FIHtrs—The following are recommended. 

A«S.1 CMne Cley — See IS:50S-1968 ' Specification for light kaolin ( first revision ) '. 

A-9.2 Berytes-^See IS : 1083-1973 ' Specification for barytas for rubber industry ( /7rsl revision ) *.

A-5.7 Carbon blacli 

A-6. Softeners — The foiiowing are recommended. 

A-6.1 Siearic Acid — See IS : 1675-1971 ' Specification for stearic acid, technical (first rev/s/on ) \ 
A-6.2 Petroleum Jelly 

A-6.3 Light Coloured Mineral Oil — for example, transformer oil [see IS : 335-1972 Specification for 
new insulating oils for transformers and switchgear ( second revision ) ]. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This Indian Standard ( Part IV) was first issued in 1971. U is now being revised to bring it in 
line with the current manufacturing practices. Values have been given in SI units. 

This standard is being issued in the following parts: 

Part I General purpose belting 
Part 11 Heat-resistant belting 
Part III Oil-resistant belting 
Part IV Hygienic belting 
It is proposed to cover PVC/piastlc hygienic belting In a separate standard. 



Reprography Unit, BIS. Nev Delhi, India
